title.narrative: Activity under preparation Financial Mechanism for Electric Buses in Costa Rica

description.narrative: Costa Rica¿s National Decarbonisation Plan 2018-2050 sets an ambitious objective for the public transport system to operate in an integrated manner, replacing the private car as the first mobility option for the population. By 2050, the Plan foresees that 100% of the buses will be zero emission.Currently, the old fleet of diesel buses circulating in the Greater Metropolitan Area (GAM) significantly contributes to air pollution and public health burdens, with the public transport sector responsible for 54% of national carbon emissions, and diesel buses alone emitting around 400 000¿tonnes of CO¿ annually. Despite the essential role of public transport in ensuring equitable access to education, employment, and healthcare, the sector faces persistent challenges related to coverage, accessibility, safety, and service quality and a significant portion of the population¿especially in the GAM where over 60% of Costa Ricans reside¿continues to experience limited or inefficient public transport services. While Costa Rica is committed to transforming its public transport system into one that is more inclusive, efficient, modern, and low-emission, the transition¿particularly the shift to clean technologies in the urban bus fleet¿is constrained by several deep-rooted structural and financial barriers. At the EU-CELAC Summit in 2023, the European Union and Costa Rica identified the conversion of the urban bus fleet to electric as an investment opportunity to be explored under the EU-LAC Global Gateway Investment Agenda, committing to work together to mobilise quality investments in the transport sector. In July 2024, the European Union, the European Investment Bank, Germany, Spain, Italy, Luxembourg, the Netherlands and Portugal (Team Europe actors), presented Costa Rica with a joint vision of the implementation of a comprehensive long-term partnership on sustainable transport. This vision ¿ represented in a package pooling technical and financial resources ¿ is designed to tackle entry barriers for European technology, while setting in motion a broader inclusive and systematic reform of public transport planning and operations. Developed around two infrastructure pillars ¿ the electric passenger train and the electrification of the bus fleet ¿ the package applies a 360-degree approach, promoting an integrated, safe, efficient and intermodal bus-train public transport service in the GAM, increasing user demand and promoting financial, environmental and socially sustainable urban mobility. As part of this package, this specific action contributes to a more sustainable, smart, efficient and safe transport system, which puts people at the centre. In particular, the action seeks to increase the adoption of European clean bus technologies to help Costa Rica reach its public policy objectives and improve financing opportunities to further scale up electrification. The action aims to address one of the main barriers for electrification ¿ access to financing. It will support the Bank of Costa Rica in setting up a trust fund to facilitate the acquisition and operation of at least 75 European electric buses through a financial leasing model through one or more Special Purpose Vehicles set up in partnership with the EU industry which has committed to implementing the Team Europe package, presented to Costa Rica in July 2024. This mechanism seeks to overcome financial barriers, reduce emissions, and promote familiarity with European standards in urban mobility, making EU technology more accessible and facilitating the transition to electric buses.The action builds on lessons learnt from past and ongoing Team Europe actions and will be accompanied by activities carried out
